day_shape: IRGC claims three tankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, CENTCOM disables St Kitts-flagged M/V Huda enforcing an Iran naval blockade, Iran executes three Karaj protesters, and Syria-Saudi sign defence pact — no UK or OFAC items.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker explosions
threads.summary: IRGC Navy public relations claimed three 'illicit' tankers on unauthorised routes exploded and burned in the Strait of Hormuz through Sunday morning, with a Sepah spokesman saying 'mines are waiting' for illicit vessels. Jerusalem Post cited Iranian state media reporting explosions heard on Qeshm Island and at Jask Port the previous evening.

threads.label: US naval blockade and interdiction
threads.summary: CENTCOM said a US military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the St Kitts-flagged M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on 7 November after the crew attempted to violate the naval blockade against Iran. Jerusalem Post reported the US military is setting up a task force to restrict Iranian weapons movement across land borders and the Caspian, while an IRGC spokesman said Tehran had prepared to withstand the blockade.

threads.label: Karaj protester executions
threads.summary: Iran executed Hassan Divobandi, Reza Zangane and Hamid Kazemi after the Supreme Court upheld death sentences tied to January protests in Karaj, IRIB and the judiciary said. Iran International and Jerusalem Post reported the three had been convicted of carrying out operations for Israel and the US during the unrest.

threads.label: Iran missile posture and Israel war warnings
threads.summary: Iran International reported the IRGC said range restrictions on ballistic missiles had been lifted, while Jerusalem Post quoted Defence Minister Katz warning of 'major challenges' and a possible Iran war. A former CENTCOM deputy commander told KAN that failure to destroy Iran's missile and drone capabilities was 'probably the most significant failure' of the war.

threads.label: Saudi-Syria pact and Yemen theatre
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Syria and Saudi Arabia signed a defence cooperation agreement during Ahmed al-Sharaa's visit to Riyadh, while a Syrian source denied plans to send troops to Yemen. Yemen's government accused the IRGC and Hezbollah of deploying 21 military operatives across six governorates, and Houthi-run Saba said Saudi airstrikes near Sanaa killed 33 and wounded 39.

threads.label: US midterms framing on Iran
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post analysis and opinion pieces weighed how the Democratic midterm win reshapes US options on Iran, from broader offensive to negotiated compromise. Defa Press framed Trump as a 'lame duck' after Republican congressional losses, and Erdogan told Trump by phone that US-Iran tensions should be resolved diplomatically.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure signals
threads.summary: Iran International reported a group of hardline women in burial shrouds rallied outside IRGC headquarters accusing the armed forces of defying Mojtaba Khamenei and demanding retaliation. Separate Iran International pieces flagged an 80% collapse in Chinese solar panel imports and government moves to delay vehicle safety rules despite 78,500 road deaths over four years.

events.title_en: Government employee salaries will not decrease with implementation of performance-based payment. Head of Civil Service and Administrative Employment Organisation: implementation of performance-based payment system does not mean reduction of employee salaries and benefits; rather, part of payments outside the employment decree for employees with more than 30 million tomans in payments outside the decree will be paid based on their performance level. This scheme was initially piloted in several organisations and has now entered the operational phase. In the first step, the Ministries of Health and Education have been included in the implementation of this scheme, and memoranda of understanding with five or six other organisations will also be signed in the coming weeks.
